key_insight: The paper proposes using a large language model as a universal AutoML searcher, jointly optimizing model architecture, training hyperparameters, and data ratios without task-specific fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Building effective ML models requires substantial manual tuning, while existing AutoML systems are often domain-specific and optimize architecture, training settings, and data ratios separately.
method: Use an LLM-based search framework to explore machine learning configurations across tasks.
Jointly optimize model architecture, training hyperparameters, and data ratios rather than treating them independently.
Introduce NCode as a unified numerical encoding; its details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: This approach could reduce manual tuning and the need for task-specific AutoML systems. The provided abstract does not include experimental results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: A central LLM searcher connected to three controls: architecture, hyperparameters, and data ratios.
A side-by-side diagram contrasting separate, domain-specific optimization with unified AutoML search.
A schematic showing the three configuration types represented through NCode.
Multiple ML task icons feeding into one shared search framework, labeled 'No task-specific fine-tuning'.
paper_title: Large Language Models as a Universal Searcher for Open-World Automated Machine Learning
paper_authors: Yuxuan Hu, Jihao Liu, Weikang Shi, Xijie Huang, Linda Wei
